thread:
Maria S.: Heads up — we're getting a spike of 503s from hosted inference in us-west1 starting ~12:30 UTC. CS reports 4 customers affected, most errors are upstream worker crashes (SIGSEGV) + container restarts.

triage-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0457. Auto-collected logs and alert group: #oncall.

Jon (oncall): I'll join. Maria, can you paste a tail of the worker logs and any dmesg / OOM killer lines?

Maria S.: Pasting condensed tail:
```
[12:29:41] infer-runner[pid=2345]: nvml: allocating 1.2G => CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[12:29:42] infer-runner[pid=2345]: attn_kernel.c:142 free(): invalid pointer
[12:29:42] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (infer-runner) score 987
[12:29:42] systemd: container exited with status 139 (SIGSEGV)
[12:29:43] k8s: restartCount++ (pod infer-runner-xyz)
```

Li: Looks like mem-fragmentation + large prefetch during batched streaming. I also see repeated cuda driver reset logs in nvme trace.

Sam R.: Which model and runtime shim? This was a recent kernel change — we rolled quant-kernels v2 at 12:10. Affected model: redwood/gpt-13b-q4 (prefetch enabled).

Abby CS: Customers reported timeouts starting 12:30; first ping from Acme at 12:31. They see 503s on generate and embed endpoints. They've asked for ETA and credits.

Jon (oncall): Mitigation idea: route heavy embed traffic off the hosted pool and into dedicated fallback; also temporarily disable prefetch on hot paths. If the change is a kernel regression, scaling up could make it worse.

Sam R.: I'm rolling a rollback of the quant-kernel patch to the us-west1 serving pool now. Rollback cmd: `deploy rollback --pool us-west1 --release 2026-04-12-quant-v1`

deploy-bot: Rollback started. Rollout ID: rb-1760054321-01. Target: 12 pods. Progress: 0/12 -> 4/12 -> 8/12 (in progress).

triage-bot: Collected artifacts: /var/log/infer-runner/*.log, dmesg, nvml-trace, kube-events. Uploaded: s3://redwood-debug/INC-2026-0457/1760054321/{logs,nvml,dmesg}. Tar: s3://.../bundle-1760054321.tgz

Li: Please capture core dump and `/proc/<pid>/maps` from the crashed worker before it's recycled. Also copy cgroup memory.limit_in_bytes and memory.usage_in_bytes. I suspect the prefetch buffer combined with kv-cache grows past usable contiguous GPU memory.

Maria S.: CS gave repro steps: large batched embed stream — 8 concurrent requests, each with ~400k tokens context and batch_size=128. They said this pattern is new after a customer-side rollout.

Sam R.: I reproduced locally using those steps against q4 runtime: memory grows linearly during kv prefetch until abort. Local logs show `attn_kernel.c:alloc_prefetch(): attempted alloc 1342177280 -> CUDA OOM` then segfault. Repro steps:
1) start runtime: `SERVE_MODE=hosted BATCH_SIZE=128 PREFETCH=on ./serve.sh`
2) send 8 parallel embed requests with ctx=400k tokens
3) observe OOM then SIGSEGV in attention kernel

Jon (oncall): Agreed plan:
- Keep rollback in flight.
- Set a short-term guard: `max_prefetch_bytes=200MB` on hosted pools.
- Route heavy embed customers to dedicated pools or queue them.
- SRE/eng-runtime to analyze coredump and confirm root cause.
- CS to provide customer-facing ETA.

Abby CS: Noted. I've informed Acme and Lambda Inc — both asked for updates ASAP. I'll offer 48h usage credit pending postmortem.

Sam R.: Tagging eng-runtime and infra: @Li please pick up core analysis once rollback stabilizes. I pushed a debug build with extra guard rails to staging.

Li: Fetching coredump now (scp from debug node). ETA ~25m to initial triage.

Maria S.: Thanks all — rollback at 11/12 pods completed, errors trending down in us-west1. I'll watch for any new crash pods and update here. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. Rollout rb-1760054321-01 -> success.

Maria S.: Update for CS: outages reduced, 503 rate back to normal baseline after rollback. Keeping incident open until Li confirms coredump analysis.

Jon (oncall): Good work. Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause, why prefetch allowed such a contiguous alloc, test coverage for large-context streams, and a short-term runtime limit (max_prefetch_bytes). Assign owners during postmortem.

Abby CS: I'll send customers a short note with the rollback summary and expected follow-up.

triage-bot: Incident INC-2026-0457 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled.

Maria S.: Closing loop here for now — will add postmortem link once Li uploads analysis.
